cases.question: How much quarterly rebate do distributors receive?
cases.answer: Rebate Policy  Eligible distributors receive a quarterly volume rebate of 2% when qualified quarterly sell-through exceeds EUR 200,000. The 2% rebate is calculated on eligible net product value after approved discounts, returns, credits, and excluded promotional items. Rebate eligibility requires valid sell-through reporting and an account in good commercial standing. Rebate calculations are reviewed after the relevant quarter closes. Disputed rebate calculations must be raised with the account manager together with supporting transaction records.. (Source: Rebate Policy)

cases.question: What information is needed for distributor onboarding?
cases.answer: Distributor Onboarding  A new distributor must complete business verification before commercial orders can be processed. Required information includes the registered company name, registration number, tax information, billing contact, shipping contact, authorized purchasing contact, and approved sales channels. The distributor account becomes active only after commercial approval is completed. Material changes to company ownership, billing information, shipping location, or authorized sales channels must be communicated to the partner account manager.. (Source: Distributor Onboarding)

cases.question: When must delivery problems be reported?
cases.answer: Delivery and Logistics  The distributor must inspect incoming shipments promptly after receipt. Delivery problems, including missing cartons, visible transport damage, incorrect quantities, or incorrect products, must be reported within 72 hours after receipt. A delivery problem report must contain the purchase order number, shipment reference, affected SKU, affected quantity, description of the problem, and supporting photographs when relevant. (Source: Delivery and Logistics)

cases.question: What warranty applies to robotic vacuum products?
cases.answer: Warranty Policy  Eligible robotic vacuum products include a two-year limited warranty from the applicable consumer purchase date, subject to the fictional terms of this demonstration handbook. Warranty service covers qualifying manufacturing defects under normal intended use. Warranty coverage does not include deliberate damage, unauthorized modification, unsupported repair, misuse, or damage caused by operation outside published product requirements. The distributor must direct warranty cases through the approved service process. (Source: Warranty Policy)

cases.question: What is required before returning products with an RMA?
cases.answer: Distributor Onboarding  A new distributor must complete business verification before commercial orders can be processed. Required information includes the registered company name, registration number, tax information, billing contact, shipping contact, authorized purchasing contact, and approved sales channels. Account credentials must not be shared with unauthorized third parties. (Source: Distributor Onboarding)

cases.question: What happens to overdue payment balances?
cases.answer: Payment Terms  Payment terms are defined in the distributor agreement and commercial account setup. Possible arrangements may include prepayment or approved credit terms. Overdue balances may result in order suspension or credit review.. (Source: Payment Terms)

cases.question: Where may distributors actively market products?
cases.answer: Geographic Sales Territory  Products may only be actively marketed and distributed within the commercial territory defined in the distributor agreement. The distributor must not intentionally redirect inventory into unauthorized geographic markets.. (Source: Geographic Sales Territory)

cases.question: What must an online marketplace listing identify?
cases.answer: Online Marketplace Policy  Sales through online marketplaces are permitted only where the marketplace or seller account is included within the distributor's approved commercial scope. Marketplace listings must accurately identify the product, condition, included accessories, and seller. Listings must not falsely imply that the distributor is the manufacturer. The distributor is responsible for marketplace customer service associated with its seller account.. (Source: Online Marketplace Policy)

cases.question: What information must purchase orders contain?
cases.answer: Purchase Orders  Commercial orders must be submitted through the approved ordering process. Each purchase order must contain the distributor account identifier, product SKU, requested quantity, billing information, shipping destination, and purchasing contact. Duplicate purchase orders must be reported immediately to the account manager.. (Source: Purchase Orders)

cases.question: How should distributors use trademarks and brand identifiers?
cases.answer: Brand Protection  The distributor must use trademarks and brand identifiers in accordance with approved brand guidelines. Suspected counterfeit products or unauthorized use of brand assets may be reported to the partner account manager. The distributor must cooperate reasonably with legitimate brand-protection investigations involving its own sales activity.. (Source: Brand Protection)
